Visitor information · Ellora Cave 16

Visiting Kailasa Temple During the Monsoon

The monsoon changes the landscape around Verul, but greenery does not imply dry surfaces, open paths or unrestricted access to the caves.

Google Maps ↗ ASI source listing ↗

Independent guide · Page reviewed 9 November 2026 · ASI listing consulted 2026-10-29

Kailasa Temple (Cave 16) is one monument within the UNESCO-listed Ellora Caves. Prices, opening status and routes are dated listings to re-check, not live confirmations.

  1. Kailasa Temple Verul
  2. Visitor information
  3. Visiting Kailasa Temple During the Monsoon

What changes in the wet season

Rain can make the surrounding scarp noticeably greener, which is part of the appeal for some visitors. At the same time, excavated stone surfaces, steps and open approaches can become wet or slippery, and low areas may hold water.

ASI describes the Ellora scarp as nearly 2 km long, so a wet-weather visit involves more exposed walking than a single monument might suggest.

Checks that matter more in the monsoon

A pleasant forecast is not evidence that a cave is open or a route is safe. Conservation work, temporary closures and local warnings can override the general ASI listing, which gives sunrise-to-sunset visiting and a weekly Tuesday closure.

  • Use the weather panel on the home page for a current regional model, not as an access or safety clearance.
  • Rely on the India Meteorological Department for official warnings.
  • Confirm current path closures and entry rules with ASI on the day.
  • Wear footwear with grip and allow extra time for slower movement.

Photography and pacing

Overcast light can be kind to carved detail, but protect equipment and avoid sheltering in closed or restricted areas. Keep the itinerary shorter than a dry-season plan, and do not extend photography beyond permitted admission hours.

Reviewed 9 November 2026. Seasonal notes are planning guidance, not a forecast or safety clearance.

Frequently asked questions

Is Kailasa Temple open during the monsoon?

The ASI listing gives sunrise-to-sunset visiting with a weekly Tuesday closure, but temporary restrictions can apply. Confirm current status with ASI before travelling.

Are the stone surfaces slippery?

Wet excavated stone and steps can be slippery. This guide has not surveyed current conditions; use grippy footwear and follow on-site instructions.

Where do I find official weather warnings?

Use the India Meteorological Department. The home-page weather panel is a regional model and is not an official warning or access clearance.
